title: Historical Parallels

parallels.statement: This bill is not about what's in it. It is about who gets to say what's in it.

historical_match.context: Senate debate on the Civil Rights Act
historical_match.quote: This is not a bill about rights. It is a bill about who decides what rights mean.

parallels.explanation: Both statements reframe a policy dispute as a procedural one. The rhetorical structure is nearly identical.

basis: The two statements share the same syntactic structure and argumentative move.
limitations: Rhetorical similarity does not imply influence or coordination.

parallels.statement: Anyone who tells you otherwise has not read the bill.

historical_match.context: House debate on the Tax Equity and Fiscal Responsibility Act
historical_match.quote: Anyone who says this bill is simple has not read it.

parallels.explanation: Dismissive framing that shifts the burden onto the opponent's preparation rather than the argument itself.

basis: Same rhetorical move; short phrase overlap.
limitations: Common phrasing; may not indicate any relationship.
